1.title: Discover, Design, Acquire and Build
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Discover, Design, Acquire and Build. It covers the exam area The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Know the purpose of discover, design, acquire and build. Define product specification, product prototype, test, continuous integration. Understand the key success metrics of the activities. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle (ten percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: Discover
1.text: Discover. Purpose: keep the product and service roadmap aligned with what consumers need and with the organization's strategy. Understand consumers and the market. interviews, feedback, demand analysis. Spot opportunities and threats. a competitor launches a new feature. Decide what to pursue. update the roadmap. Typical success metrics: consumer satisfaction with ideas, share of roadmap items with a clear value case.

1.title: Design
1.text: Design. Purpose: turn validated needs into a product specification, architecture and prototypes that can be built. Product specification. A written description of what the product must be and do (features, quality, limits). Product prototype. An early, working or visual model used to test ideas with users before full build. Exam tip: Specification equals the description. Prototype equals the early model to test. Both are produced in design. Typical success metrics: stakeholder approval of designs, share of designs validated with users.

1.title: Acquire
1.text: Acquire. Purpose: secure and allocate the resources needed to build the product: people, tools, hardware, software, services, licenses. Acquire covers buying, hiring, renting or licensing, and managing the suppliers involved. Typical success metrics: resources available when needed, cost against budget.

1.title: Build
1.text: Build. Purpose: create, configure and test the technology and components that make up the product or service. Test. Checking that a component or product meets its requirements and works correctly. Continuous integration (C I). Frequently merging code changes into a shared place with automatic build and test. Typical success metrics: defects found before release, build and test cycle time. Exam tip: C I equals merge often and test automatically. (Continuous delivery and deployment are in Module seven.).

1.title: Build, continued
1.text: Build. The figure shows this: Discover, design, acquire and build: purpose and key outputs. Exam tip: Match the verb to the activity: find out is discover, specify and prototype is design, get resources is acquire, create and test is build.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which activity keeps the roadmap aligned with consumer needs and organizational strategy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Discover. That is the purpose of discover.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team produces an early clickable model and tests it with five users. Which term applies? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Product prototype. A prototype is an early model used to test ideas.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statement about the build activity is C O R R E C T? (one) It creates, configures and tests the product. (two) It includes testing against requirements. (three) It decides the strategic direction of the organization. (four) It restores service after an incident. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and two. Build creates, configures and tests.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). blank is the practice of frequently merging code changes with automatic build and test. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Continuous integration. Continuous integration merges often and tests automatically.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A product manager secures developers, cloud licenses and a testing tool for a new product. Which activity is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Acquire. Acquire secures and allocates resources.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which output belongs to the design activity? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A product specification. Design produces specifications, architectures and prototypes.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of discover? Answer: To keep the roadmap aligned with consumer needs and strategy. Question two. What is a product specification? Answer: A written description of what the product must be and do. Question three. What is a product prototype? Answer: An early model used to test ideas before the full build.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does acquire do? Answer: Secures and allocates the resources needed to build. Question five. What does build do? Answer: Creates, configures and tests the product. Question six. What is continuous integration? Answer: Frequently merging code with automatic build and test.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Activity: Purpose Key terms. Discover: align roadmap with needs and strategy consumer needs. Design: needs into specification and prototypes product specification, prototype. Acquire: secure resources people, tools, suppliers. Build: create, configure, test test, continuous integration.
